Belgium / CITY EDIT

Ten cities.
Very different weekends.

Choose a break by mood, scale and travel time. These cities are starting points, not a ranking.

01 / Belgium

Brussels

Brussels combines ornate guildhall architecture with Art Nouveau heritage and European institutions.

Explore Brussels ↗02 / Belgium

Bruges

Bruges preserves a medieval streetscape of canals, stepped-gable houses and historic squares.

Explore Bruges ↗03 / Belgium

Ghent

Ghent combines medieval towers and canal-side guildhouses with the energy of a university city.

Explore Ghent ↗04 / Belgium

Antwerp

Antwerp brings together a major port's trading heritage, Flemish art and contemporary fashion.

Explore Antwerp ↗05 / Belgium

Leuven

Leuven's university heritage shapes a compact centre of historic colleges, squares and cafés.

Explore Leuven ↗06 / Belgium

Mechelen

Mechelen combines a cathedral-dominated skyline with historic palaces and streets along the River Dyle.

Explore Mechelen ↗07 / Belgium

Liège

Liège spreads along the Meuse beneath steep historic hillsides and monumental stairways.

Explore Liège ↗08 / Belgium

Namur

Namur sits beneath a hillside citadel where the Sambre and Meuse rivers meet.

Explore Namur ↗09 / Belgium

Mons

Mons combines a historic central square with a distinctive Baroque belfry and a strong cultural tradition.

Explore Mons ↗10 / Belgium

Tournai

Tournai's skyline is defined by its five-towered cathedral and Belgium's oldest belfry.

Explore Tournai ↗
